rulers.note: Offered the leadership in 1523; he died on 14 June 1571 (text) or 6 July 1571 (infobox). Terumoto's father Takamoto 'died suddenly' in 1563; his tenure is not on the pages and Motonari 'supervised clan affairs'.

rulers.name: Mōri Terumoto
rulers.title: head of the clan
rulers.note: Heir 1563, command 1564; Lord of Hiroshima 1589-1600; 1.2 million koku at the peak; cut to Nagato and Suō in 1600; retired 1623, died 2 June 1625.

rulers.name: Mōri Hidenari
rulers.title: daimyō

correction.text: the Mōri home domain around Yoshida-Kōriyama in Aki

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a daimyo domain Cliopatria lacks (Warring States Japan draws all of Japan as one shape). Motonari was born in 'a small domain of Aki' and offered the leadership in 1523 at Yoshida-Kōriyama; he beat Takeda Motoshige at Arita-Nakaide in 1517. A 20 km circle at Yoshida (about 1,260 km2) stands for the home domain; the pages do not date the spread across Aki.

By 1550 Motonari 'had Bingo Province, with the Kobayakawa clan supporting him' and 'held Iwami Province with the Kikkawa clan' (Motonari page); the clan page: he expanded 'across Aki'. Hiroshima Prefecture (40 cells) and western Shimane stand in; in 1556 Amago Haruhisa captured Yamabuki Castle and the Iwami silver mine, not drawn. 1 October 1555: Miyajima.

correction.text: Aki, Bingo, Iwami, Suō and Nagato

keyframe_review.note: 1557: Ōuchi Yoshinaga forced to suicide; 'years longer to completely bring Suo province and Nagato province under Mōri's control' (page; no year for the full conquest). Yamaguchi Prefecture (26 cells) stands for the two provinces.

1558: 'Mōri captured Moji castle from the Ōuchi'; Sōrin retook it in September 1559 and the Mōri 'quickly took the castle again'; an Ōtomo assault failed in 1561. A 30 km circle on the Buzen coast (about 2,000 km2) stands for the holding; the page does not name Buzen.

correction.text: the Mōri lands of 1571, 1.2 million koku at the peak

keyframe_review.note: 1571: Terumoto inherited lands 'that stretched from Buzen on Kyushu to the borders of Harima and Bizen'; the peak was 1.2 million koku. Bitchū (Takamatsu Castle, 1582) is the only eastern province the pages name; a 30 km circle stands for it (confidence 1). The clan page's 'four eastern provinces' lost in 1600 are not named, so the shape under-draws the eastern Chūgoku (Hōki, Mimasaka, parts of Bizen), and the Buzen remainder is not drawn. 1583: vassal of Hideyoshi (Toyotomi dossier).

1600: after Sekigahara Ieyasu left Terumoto 'only Nagato and Suō Provinces, worth 369,000 koku' (Terumoto page); Chōshū Domain 'established' 1600, Hagi Castle; 1871 abolished into Yamaguchi Prefecture. The branch domains Iwakuni (60,000 koku), Chōfu (50,000), Tokuyama (40,000) and Kiyosue (10,000) lie inside and are not drawn separately.

region.text: the Mōri home domain around Yoshida-Kōriyama in Aki

ledger.note: 1523: Kōmatsumaru died; 'The senior Mōri vassals met and decided to offer the leadership to Motonari' (10 August entry to Yoshida-Kōriyama).
By 1550: the clan page says Motonari 'expanded the clan's power across Aki'; he beat Takeda Motoshige at Arita-Nakaide in 1517. The pages give no year for the Aki spread; bridged, confidence 1.
By 1550: 'Motonari had Bingo Province, with the Kobayakawa clan supporting him' (the page gives no event year).
Around 1550: 'Motonari held Iwami Province with the Kikkawa clan'; in 1556 Amago Haruhisa captured Yamabuki Castle and the Iwami silver mine.

1557: 'it would take the Mōri until 1557 to force Ōuchi Yoshinaga to commit suicide and years longer to completely bring Suo province and Nagato province under Mōri's control'. Miyajima was fought on 1 October 1555 (page). The year is the page's; the full control is later and undated.
1558: 'Mōri captured Moji castle from the Ōuchi.' The page gives September 1559 for Sōrin's retaking and the Mōri's quick recapture.
1558: the Moji front against Ōtomo Sōrin begins (the page: Sōrin retook the castle in September 1559; an Ōtomo assault failed in 1561).

ledger.note: 1562: 'Motonari invaded Izumo', beginning the second siege of Toda Castle (1562-1563); 'Amago Yoshihisa later surrendered'.

region.text: Izumo Province and the Oki islands: eastern Shimane Prefecture

ledger.note: 1566: 'The Amago clan, the Mōri's traditional rival, had been destroyed' (Terumoto page); in 1570 Amago Katsuhisa was beaten at Fubeyama and fled to Oki.

region.text: Izumo Province and the Oki islands: eastern Shimane Prefecture

ledger.note: 1566: the Amago destroyed. The Terumoto page does not name Izumo and gives no 1566-1570 conquest; the Motonari page names the 1562 Izumo invasion.
1569: Ōuchi Teruhiro's rebellion beaten in October; 'The Mōri lost influence in Chikuzen and most Buzen bases'; the Sōrin page: Tatarahama 1569, Tachibana castle retaken by the Ōtomo.
October 1569: 'most Buzen bases' lost. The Terumoto page's 1571 sentence still has the lands stretching 'from Buzen on Kyushu'.
1571: the lands 'stretched from Buzen on Kyushu to the borders of Harima and Bizen'. The page names no eastern province; Bitchū is bridged from Takamatsu Castle (1582), confidence 1.

1576-1578: the Mōri intervened in the Ishiyama Hongan-ji War (First Battle of Kizugawaguchi, 1576); 'Kōzuki Castle in Harima was besieged' in 1577-1578; the Honganji surrendered in 1580. The Oda dossier starts the Chūgoku campaign in 1577.

1582: Hideyoshi besieged Takamatsu Castle in Bitchū; 'After Honnōji, the Mōri made peace with Hideyoshi'; the page lists no lands ceded. In 1583 Terumoto became Hideyoshi's vassal (the Toyotomi dossier carries the tint).
1589: Terumoto is 'Lord of Hiroshima' 1589-1600 (succession table); the page says he built Hiroshima Castle and gives no date.

union.text: Izumo Province and the Oki islands: eastern Shimane Prefecture

ledger.note: 1600: 'After Sekigahara, Ieyasu reduced his domains, leaving him only Nagato and Suō Provinces, worth 369,000 koku in total'; Terumoto had nominally led the Western Army (clan page). The clan page: 'lost four eastern provinces'.
1600: Chōshū Domain 'established', based at Hagi Castle in Nagato; the clan's holdings cut from 1,200,000 to 369,000 koku. Same house; the Edo han.
1600: the capital moves from Hiroshima to Hagi (clan page; Chōshū page: based at Hagi Castle in Nagato).
1862: 'Hagi Castle's status as capital ended, and Yamaguchi Castle became the capital (1862-1871).'
1871: 'the han system was abolished, and the domain's territory was absorbed into Yamaguchi Prefecture.'

wars.outcome: Motonari sailed out on 1 October 1555 in a thunderstorm; Ōuchi Yoshinaga was forced to suicide in 1557.
wars.note: The page names no Ōuchi commander.

wars.name: Mōri conquest of Suō and Nagato
wars.outcome: Yoshinaga's suicide in 1557; years more to bring Suō and Nagato fully under control (no year on the page).

wars.name: Mōri–Ōtomo war in Buzen
wars.outcome: Moji changed hands in 1558-1559; the Mōri lost most Buzen bases in 1569.

wars.name: Mōri conquest of Izumo

zones.text: Izumo Province and the Oki islands: eastern Shimane Prefecture

wars.outcome: The Toda siege of 1562-1563; the Amago destroyed by 1566; Katsuhisa beaten at Fubeyama in 1570 and fled to Oki.

wars.outcome: Takamatsu was besieged in 1582; the Mōri made peace with Hideyoshi after Honnōji and became his vassals in 1583.

wars.outcome: The Chōshū army used a flag during the war (page); the pages give no start or end year or battles.

sources.title: Mōri clan
sources.note: Home Aki; Motonari expanded across Aki and into neighbouring provinces, nearly all of the Chugoku region; Sekigahara 1600 Terumoto nominally led the Western Army, the clan lost four eastern provinces and moved its capital from Hiroshima to Hagi, the new fief Nagato and Suo, later Choshu Domain; Terumoto first daimyo of Hiroshima Domain, Hidenari first daimyo of Choshu, Takachika 13th and last.

sources.title: Mōri Motonari
sources.note: 1523 offered the leadership; 1517 Arita-Nakaide; allegiance to the Ouchi 1525-1554; by 1550 Bingo (Kobayakawa) and Iwami (with the Kikkawa); 1 Oct 1555 Miyajima; 1557 Ouchi Yoshinaga forced to suicide, Suo and Nagato brought under control years longer; 1556 Iwami silver mine lost to the Amago; 1558 Moji taken, retaken by Sorin Sept 1559 and again by the Mori; 1562 Izumo invaded, Toda siege 1562-1563; died 1571.

sources.title: Mōri Terumoto

sources.title: Chōshū Domain
sources.note: 1600 established at Hagi Castle in Nagato, holdings cut from 1,200,000 to 369,000 koku; branch domains Iwakuni, Chofu, Tokuyama, Kiyosue; 1862 Yamaguchi Castle became the capital (1862-1871); 1868-1869 Boshin War flag; 1871 abolished, absorbed into Yamaguchi Prefecture.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from four pages (Mōri clan, Mōri Motonari, Mōri Terumoto, Chōshū Domain). A Sengoku daimyo house that continues as the Chōshū han inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row and then the Tokugawa shogunate row; identity runs 1523-1871 with a 1600 rename to Chōshū Domain. Dated by the pages: Aki (1523 home domain; spread undated), Bingo and Iwami (by 1550), Suō and Nagato (1557, full control undated), Moji (1558, lost 1569), Izumo (1562 invasion, Amago destroyed by 1566), the 1.2 million koku peak (late 16th century), the 1600 cut to Nagato and Suō, capitals Hiroshima 1589, Hagi 1600, Yamaguchi 1862. Not on the pages and not drawn: Hōki, Mimasaka, Bizen, Oki detail (inside eastern Shimane), the four 'eastern provinces' lost in 1600 (named only as a number on the clan page), the Buzen remainder after 1569, and Iyo (the Mōri generals held Iyo after 1585, see the Toyotomi dossier). Page conflicts: Motonari's death is 14 June 1571 (text) or 6 July 1571 (infobox); the clan page's infobox says the clan ruled until 1868 and is 'still extant'; the clan page puts the Hiroshima-to-Hagi move at Sekigahara while the Terumoto page does not name a capital. The Boshin War is dated only by the flag (1868-1869). The Toyotomi dossier carries the 1583 vassal tint for Terumoto and its end in 1600. The branch domains (Iwakuni, Chōfu, Tokuyama, Kiyosue) are inside Yamaguchi and not modelled. Counterpart strings: 'otomo-clan', 'oda-clan', 'toyotomi-clan', 'tokugawa-shogunate', 'empire-of-japan' exist; the rest are clans or lords named on the pages. Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
